notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Isaiah 36 this time, because I never got to read a single source page.

My first step tried to open eight commentary pages at once: Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit, Barnes, Jamieson-Fausset-Brown, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes. That request hit the research tool's usage limit before any page loaded. When I tried to open just the Enduring Word page, I'd used up all my tool calls for this turn. Your rules say I can only report what the pages actually say and must give a URL for every point. Writing commentary from memory would break both, so I've left everything out.

**What I'll do next turn,** if you send a short follow-up (e.g., "continue"), opening the pages one or two at a time:

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:**
   - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-36/
   - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/isaiah/36.htm
   - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/isaiah/36.htm
   - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/isaiah/36.htm
   - https://www.preceptaustin.org/isaiah-36-commentary
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, Spurgeon sermons on spurgeon.org, and Reformed sources on ligonier.org and monergism.com. The likely topics are v. 7 (Hezekiah removing the high places) and v. 21 (the people staying silent).
3. **Other views:**
   - Modern scholarship: the NET Bible notes and bibleodyssey.org on Sennacherib, Lachish and the Rabshakeh's speech.
   - Catholic and Orthodox: newadvent.org and catholic.com.
   - Popular modern teaching (prosperity, word of faith, hyper-grace): I'll include this only if the allowed sites actually discuss it for this chapter.

If you'd like a smaller first batch, tell me which part to start with, such as Enduring Word and Ellicott only.
